prize_parts.citation: For the development of the catalytic, ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling reaction

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B068 for Buchwald and Hartwig. Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is the most mature and most cleanly attributed achievement on the shortlist. The decisive advance was a general catalytic method built on mechanistic understanding of oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination, with successive ligand generations that extended scope to nearly any amine and aryl partner. It has about thirty years of independent confirmation and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. On the chair's question about the 2010 prize: that prize honoured C-C bond formation by Heck, Negishi and Suzuki. C-N coupling is not a substrate extension of those reactions. Amine binding, the competing beta-hydride elimination and the difficult C-N reductive elimination are different mechanistic problems, and they were solved by new ligand design, not by transferring existing conditions. On Kosugi, the citation should say 'catalytic, ligand-controlled' so that the stoichiometric organotin precedent is distinguished by the wording and does not need a third name. Two independent groups gave the general version in parallel, which suits a two-person prize.
statement.case_against: The 2010 proximity objection is real for members who treat cross-coupling as one recognised family, and a committee that holds that view will not be moved by my mechanistic argument alone. B068 also has the narrowest opening support among the leading options. Targeted protein degradation (B057) has five stated supporters and is the broadest new modality on the list, and I cannot dismiss the possibility that the committee wants to honour a new mode of action. My scepticism about B057 rests on timing and credit. No degrader is approved, and three names cannot fairly cover the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages. That scepticism does not make B057 a poor choice, and I would find it defensible if the committee judges the confirmed mechanism and the late-stage trials sufficient.

responses.point: The chair argues that the committee has not traditionally required an approved drug when mechanism and generality are confirmed in many laboratories, and that Crews, Deshaies and Handa span concept and mechanism, while granting that the cut is not settled.
responses.response: This is a fair point on precedent and it weakens my timing objection. I accept that an approved drug is not a formal requirement, and the mechanism and reproducibility are not in doubt. My remaining objection is to the cut. A citation that joins the PROTAC concept to the cereblon mechanism joins two discoveries with different histories, and you yourself say the cut is not settled. I would ask the members who support B057 to decide first whether this is one achievement or two. If it is two, the three-name limit cannot honour it, and I think that is a real weakness and not just a presentational one. If it is one, the citation should say precisely what it recognises.

responses.point: Brzezinski argues that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs rational and drug-like, and that Handa belongs to the glue lineage, so the third name is unresolved.
responses.response: I agree with Brzezinski's attribution analysis, and it is the reason I put Ciulli in my own opening proposal. Structural work on the ternary complex is what turned PROTACs from a proof of concept into a design problem. I also see Aqvist's and Linke's argument that dropping Handa leaves glues without a founder. Neither trio is clean, and I think this is evidence that B057 is not yet in a form that avoids a visibly arbitrary choice. A PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli would be coherent but would not cover cereblon. A three-person set with Handa covers both strands but leaves out the structural chemistry. I do not see an answer in the record that I would call defensible without reservation.

responses.point: Aili argues that ternary-complex formation and degradation kinetics are well characterised and independently confirmed, so the maturity worry is partly answered, and that B068 is a refinement within a class honoured in 2010.
responses.response: I accept the first part. The biochemistry is solid, and that moves me towards treating the timing question as a matter of judgment and not as a flaw in B057. I do not accept the description of B068 as a refinement. The reaction forms a different bond, through different intermediates, and needed its own ligand families. Sakamoto, Ciulli and Handa have comparable claims, so B057 carries more attribution risk than B068, which has two clear names. I would also say that maturity and clean credit count in favour of a prize, whatever the novelty of the mode of action.

responses.point: Chabes holds that B057 is a new chemical modality and that B054 is the more mature fallback if the committee judges degradation premature. He accepts that B068 is mature but sees it as an extension of a recognised class.
responses.response: I appreciate that Chabes lets B057 and B054 stand on mechanism and maturity respectively. On the fallback question from the chair, I now regard B054 as a stronger fallback than I did in round 1, since five members name it as an alternative and none disputes its quality, so I add it to my alternatives. My concern about B054 is that credit is diffuse. Mehl and Yokoyama are excluded and there was no single decisive demonstration, and with the 2018, 2020 and 2024 prizes it may look like another biomolecular-tool award. Those concerns are real, though smaller than the B057 attribution problem.

responses.point: Somfai notes that Kosugi's tin-amide reaction needed stoichiometric toxic organotin reagents and was narrow in scope, and that the 2010 prize recognised C-C coupling.
responses.response: I agree, and the point answers the chair's question on Kosugi. The prize should recognise the catalytic, general method, and I will propose the citation wording to say so. I do not want to rest our case on a bias for methodology. The strongest case for B068 is clean credit and thirty years of confirmed practice, and the committee should weigh it against the conceptual novelty of B057 on those terms. If the committee decides that C-N coupling is too close to 2010, I will accept that.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges C-N coupling distinct enough from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands are one achievement or two, and whether Handa or Ciulli should take the third B057 place.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay B057, and whether B054 is a better-supported fallback than B068 if neither reaches five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No change. No shortlisted candidate has a documented tie to me, to Stockholm University or to my own work in electron crystallography. I am a Stockholm University colleague of the Secretary, Peter Brzezinski, which bears on no candidate. I request no recusal and see no recusal need for any other member.
